items.title: 67520_George Handy oral history interview
items.q: I joined Jack Teagarden; I stayed with him for about a year, toured the South, had a ball with him.

ctx.x: I was playing with the band. I wrote a few things probably; I don't remember. I usually write something for every band I've ever been with.

Then I joined--where was this--this was right after I came out of the army, that was '41, '42, probably just the band before Raeburn, I joined Jack Teagarden; I stayed with him for about a year, toured the South, had a ball with him. There was a player, I loved to hear him play.

One of the big thrills of my life was the beginning of every night working with Jack Teagarden, just to hear him pick up the horn and play his theme, 'I've Got a Right to Sing the Blues'. It's hard to describe, I just got such a warm feeling when he would start that.
